subject: Private VPC - transient controllink handshake jitter during node-pool rolling update
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Karen Liu <karen.liu@nexahealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:23:12Z
Subject: Brief: transient controllink jitter during your rolling update (NexaHealth)

Hi Samir / Karen,

We observed a transient connectivity spike affecting controllink traffic for your Private VPC during a Redwood node-pool rolling update this morning (approx 07:45–08:10 PDT). Symptoms: 5–12% increased 5xx from the management API and a small number of customer-hosted agents briefly re-establishing TLS sessions. Data plane inference requests remained healthy; we did not detect any data exfiltration or model-state inconsistency.

Immediate actions we took:
- Paused the rolling update at 07:53 PDT to prevent further exposure.
- Shifted control-plane routing to the secondary conductor in us-west-2 to reduce handshake pressure.
- Captured handshake traces and agent logs (attached).

Next steps we propose:
1) Short bridge with your ops team — can we do 11:00 PDT today?
2) We'll share the initial traces and a recommended mitigation to extend controllink handshake timeout and proceed with a guarded incremental rollout.

I know uptime here is critical; we're treating this as priority P1 for the duration of the follow-up. Apologies for the impact — we'll get you a full timeline and root-cause follow-up within 24 hours after today's bridge.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-15T09:10:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Brief: transient controllink jitter — internal coordination

Team — forwarding customer confirmation and logs. TL;DR: node-pool rolling upgrade correlated with a spike in TLS handshake resets on the controllink. Initial trace look: bulk of resets occurred during KV cache warmup when the agent attempted back-to-back re-establishes.

Initial theory: a timing regression introduced in agent 1.4.2 (keepalive interval change) interacting with our conductor backpressure algorithm caused transient handshake jitter under concurrent restarts. This isn't a data-plane corruption issue, but it led to control-plane request failures.

Action items I want covered before the 11:00 bridge:
- Irene: can you confirm whether we saw the same handshake failure pattern in prior canary runs?
- Marissa: compile the EVA traces and redact any sensitive fields; prepare a short summary slide.
- Ben: prepare a rollback plan for node-pool 1.4.2 -> 1.4.1 and estimated time-to-recover.

Attaching current traces for your review (controllink-handshake-traces.zip).

Karthik
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@nexahealth.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@nexahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T12:05:20Z
Subject: Post-bridge summary & immediate mitigations — NexaHealth Private VPC incident (09/15)

Hi Samir / Karen,

Thanks for joining the bridge. Quick summary and agreed actions:

1) Timeline (UTC):
- 07:44 — 07:53 PDT: rolling update of node-pool initiated in your us-west-2 control region.
- 07:48 — 07:58 PDT: transient spike in controllink TLS handshake resets; management API error rate rose to ~8% for ~10 minutes.
- 07:53 PDT: Redwood ops paused the rolling update and diverted controllink traffic to secondary conductor.

2) Root-cause (most likely):
- A timing change in agent 1.4.2 (reduced keepalive retransmit backoff) combined with concurrent restart behavior caused bursts of near-simultaneous TLS re-negotiations. Under that burst, a small portion of the conductor connection pool reached ephemeral resource contention and led to handshake failures.
- Importantly: this affected only the control channel (management/telemetry). Inference/data-plane requests continued to be served by warmed inference workers and did not encounter model state divergence.

3) Immediate mitigations agreed on bridge:
- Apply a conservative handshake timeout extension (increase from 2s -> 6s) on the conductor and agent side for the next 24h.
- Proceed with a canaryed rolling restart of remaining nodes with a 10% concurrency cap.
- Re-run the failing node-pool upgrade in our staging mirror to validate.

4) Action items and owners:
- Redwood (Irene): patch handshake timeout and validate in staging — ETA 2 hours.
- Redwood (Ben): rollback playbook ready in case further instability — ready in 30 minutes.
- NexaHealth (Samir): share any additional agent logs if you find edge cases — requested by EOD.

5) Evidence & artifacts:
- Attached: controllink-handshake-traces.zip (sanitized), nexa_ops_log_snippet.txt.
- Jira: NEXA-472 (link below) has the running timeline and attachments.

6) Customer ask:
- Please confirm whether the extended handshake timeout and the planned guarded rollout are acceptable. We recognize the friction here and will coordinate a precise maintenance window if you want firm control over timing.

We'll follow up with a formal postmortem and a set of preventive controls (canary telemetry, updated rollout policy, and alert thresholds) within 48 hours.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Technical Program Lead, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Date: 2026-09-16T10:00:00Z
Subject: Postmortem + next steps and customer credit proposal — NexaHealth controllink jitter (09/15)

Hi Samir / Karen,

Following our bridge and the validation patch we applied, here's the agreed post-incident summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption.

Summary:
- What happened: A timing regression in agent 1.4.2 combined with concurrent node restarts caused short-lived bursts of TLS handshake re-negotiations against the conductor, creating ephemeral connection resource contention and 5xx on the management API. No inference/data loss or model-state divergence was observed.
- Impact window: ~07:48–07:58 PDT on 2026-09-15.
- Scope: Control-plane only; limited to your us-west-2 region where the rolling update executed.

Remediation completed:
- We patched the conductor and agent configs to extend handshake timeouts and validated the patch in our staging mirror.
- Performed a controlled, low-concurrency resume of the rollout with a 10% concurrency cap — completed successfully on 2026-09-15 at 14:30 PDT.

Preventive measures (short-term):
- Canary telemetry: adding a handshake-failure SLO alert that will trigger at >=3% sustained 5xx over 5 minutes during upgrades.
- Rollout guardrails: enforce concurrency caps for node-pool upgrades and require successful staging mirror run before production resume.

Preventive measures (long-term):
- Update agent release checklist to include explicit keepalive/backoff compatibility tests against the conductor pool.
- Improve connection pool backpressure algorithm to better tolerate bursts of re-negotiation.

Customer goodwill: as a gesture for the incident and the operational overhead you incurred, Redwood will apply a one-week service credit to your September invoice. If you'd prefer a technical review session instead, we're happy to schedule a 60-minute architecture deep-dive with our runtime team.

Open asks:
- Please confirm acceptance of the credit or preference for a technical review.
- If you saw any residual anomalies on your side after 09/15 15:00 PDT, please share logs and we'll correlate.

We've attached the postmortem draft and the sanitized traces for your records (postmortem-draft-20260916.pdf). If you'd like this converted into a SOC2-friendly artifact, we can produce an executive summary and evidence bundle.

Thanks again for the quick coordination — we value NexaHealth's partnership and will incorporate the learnings across our private deployment fleet.

Best,
